mechanism.what: lane2's post-archive.test.ts opens with beforeEach(prisma.post.deleteMany({})). vitest.config.ts sets no fileParallelism, so test files run in parallel workers, and .env points all of them at one file:/workspace/repo/prisma/dev.db. lane2's wipe races lane1's fixtures.
evidence: lane1's 'get posts by author' expected 2 and received 0
lane1's other author test, 'pagination for posts by author', passed in the same run
no shared procedure: lane1 added byAuthor, lane2 added archive
mechanism.claim_map_note: the recorded chain postRouter -> defaultPostSelect is true of the two patches and says nothing about the mechanism. No analysis of TypeScript identifiers finds 'these two test files race on one sqlite file'.

claim.chain_note: what the claim map emitted, and it is not the mechanism

mechanism_named_by_claim_map.why: the chain is `postRouter -> defaultPostSelect`, a true statement about two patches that touch the same router. The mechanism is that both lanes' test files run in parallel vitest workers against one sqlite file, and lane2's `beforeEach(prisma.post.deleteMany({}))` wipes lane1's fixtures. The shared thing is a database, not an identifier, and no static analysis of TypeScript names finds it.

published_surface.why: not applicable: both lanes are inside one application and no package boundary is crossed
published_surface.note: CE-004 gave the rule that publication puts a call site beyond the provider's reach, and CE-006 showed concurrency does the same without a package. CE-007 is a third way: the shared thing is not a call site at all. Neither lane called the other's code. They shared a mutable resource that neither brief mentions and no import graph contains.

prediction.frozen: the same, 1 or 2 of 5, and NOT lower. This is the load-bearing one. The room is generated from the BASE tree before either lane starts, so it can describe what is already claimed and cannot describe what the other lane is doing right now. Read c06b's room.md: it lists `add` among the route names already registered and says nothing whatever about that procedure's input shape, because at the moment the room was written the shape had not changed. CE-006's failure is concurrent by construction, and a static room is structurally blind to it. If the roomed arm ships materially fewer semantic failures, that prediction is wrong and the room is doing something I cannot account for.
prediction.observed: one semantic failure in five roomed episodes; bare shipped none. Fisher two-sided p = 1.000.
prediction.note: the frozen prediction was that the roomed arm would not ship fewer than bare, because the room is generated from the base tree and cannot describe what the other lane is doing concurrently. It shipped one and bare shipped none.

repair.verdict: the engine flagged the correct symptom -- the branches merge cleanly and the combined tree fails -- the roomed repair round ran, and the merged tree failed identically afterwards.

caveats: It is a race. vitest.config.ts sets no fileParallelism, so test files run in parallel workers, and .env points every one at file:/workspace/repo/prisma/dev.db. Timing decides the outcome.
Any future semantic failure on this repository has to be checked against the shared database before being called a contract failure. CE-007 needed that check; CE-006 passed it.

matched_control.differs_in: the arm, and nothing else -- same task, same two briefs, same model, same sandbox
matched_control.why_it_is_the_control: Ten episodes produced exactly two clean merges. A clean merge is the only state in which a semantic failure is possible, so the informative comparison is not roomed-against-bare but this clean merge against the other one: two lanes merged cleanly and the product was right, two lanes merged cleanly and it was wrong.
